# 本次素材生成紀錄

最終補充：有機狀態統一使用 organic-wildlife.png 的小鳥與兩隻蝴蝶疊圖；取代早期簡單方塊提示。以下是其內建 imagegen 生成描述：

Use case: stylized-concept. A single transparent sprite atlas for the organic-farming overlay in a Sanxia Taiwanese tea-garden 16-bit pixel-art game. Exact two equal square cells side by side, 2:1 total image. Left cell: one friendly small Taiwan-style native brown-and-cream songbird with a slightly blue-grey wing, dark eye, tiny golden beak and clearly visible slender feet, facing left, perched on a very small twig. Right cell: two small butterflies, one creamy white and one golden yellow, open wings with a few dark brown pixel markings and slender dark bodies, friendly natural silhouettes. Both cells must use precisely the same crisp, detailed tiny square-pixel cluster style and thin dark outlines as richly drawn isometric tea plantation terrain, consistent pixel scale, flat clustered pixel shading with three to five color values, no vector smoothing, no painterly gradients, no glow. Clear silhouettes that remain recognizable when each cell is rendered only 35 pixels wide. Objects centered with generous fully transparent margins, no overlap between cells, no labels, no letters, no scenery, no tea plants, no ground, no border frame. Alpha transparency outside the bird/twig and butterflies.

工具：內建 imagegen。地景、混作採透明背景；成果卡採不透明背景。最終仍由 HTML 顯示文字。

## 實際使用的素材

- terrain-unified-v2.png：統一土地基底，4 × 6 格。
- terrain-erosion-light.png、terrain-erosion-severe.png：相同布局的兩級土壤流失版本。
- intercrop-overlays-v1.png：白色柚花、金黃金桔。
- intercrop-erosion.png：兩種混作的輕度、嚴重受損外觀；實際圖像分界經檢查採 55% 高度裁切。
- achievement-atlas.png：六張初始成果圖卡。
- achievement-volunteer.png：打工換宿成果圖卡。

96 種基本組合乘上 3 種流失狀態，共 288 種；完整檢查入口為 dist/art-audit.html。原有素材檔保留，主遊戲只載入上述新版與 mountain-world.png。Canvas 以像素插值繪製，框架也採硬邊像素風格。圖集邊緣採一致裁切留白，避免相鄰格殘影。

## 統一地景生成描述

Use case: stylized-concept. ONE unified production terrain sprite atlas for a Taiwanese Sanxia tea farming pixel-art game. Exact uniform 4-column by 6-row grid, 24 equal rectangular cells. The entire image should be wide 4:3, each cell wide 2:1. Every cell contains one complete isolated isometric diamond land block. ALL 24 cells MUST share the same hard pixel-cluster 16-bit art style, identical pixel scale, diamond footprint width, fixed camera, palette, light from upper left, coarse warm grey stone, ochre soil and dark green outlines. Transparent alpha background throughout, generous clear transparent margins within EACH cell, no crossing or overlap between cells, no scenery background or shadows outside blocks. No text, no arrows, no labels, no flowers, fruit, insects or birds; those are separate overlays. Crisp visible square pixels, not painterly or smooth vector. These tiles replace all previous terrain art, consistency is paramount.
ROWS 1-4: sixteen tea garden terrain blocks. Columns change terrain geometry: column1 normal unengineered sloping tea garden with ONE low perimeter wall and NO terrace steps. Column2 true multi-level terrace: high at REAR RIGHT, four broad stone retaining-wall steps descend toward FRONT LEFT. Column3 true multi-level terrace: high at REAR LEFT, steps descend toward FRONT RIGHT. Column4 true multi-level terrace: high at REAR CENTER, steps descend toward FRONT CENTER facing viewer. The actual stone risers and elevation must follow those directions; do not just rotate tea rows on flat ground.
Row1: bright rounded Qingxin Ganzai tea bushes with curled oval bright green leaves; EXPOSED brown soil between rows, no grass. Row2: same Ganzai tea but thick low GRASS covering the soil between rows and on the steps. Row3: Qingxin Oolong tea bushes with slender elongated leaves and DARK forest-green foliage, sparse tiny purple new shoots, exposed brown soil between rows. Row4: same dark Oolong tea with thick low GRASS between rows and on steps.
ROW5 four environment blocks, same footprint and style: column1 preserved forest with several mature native broadleaf trees and green ground; column2 grassland meadow with NO tea bushes; column3 eroded tea plot with thin sickly tea bushes and brown rills of visibly washed-away topsoil; column4 collapsed hillside debris block with exposed broken earth, scattered grey stones and a disrupted retaining wall, NO healthy crops.
ROW6 four young tea seedling blocks, normal unengineered geometry (NOT terrace): column1 young Ganzai seedlings on bare brown soil; column2 same young Ganzai with grass between seedlings; column3 young Oolong seedlings with narrow dark leaves on bare soil; column4 same young Oolong with grass between seedlings. Make seedlings small and sparse, visibly different from mature bushes.
Important: all base tea terrain has ONLY tea and either bare soil or grass, absolutely NO citrus trees or blossoms, because the game overlays those separately. Match the cheerful detailed isometric pixel art used for lush Taiwanese mountain tea gardens, with a readable silhouette even when reduced to a 180-pixel-wide in-game tile. Make every cell centered consistently with identical extents so automatic slicing works.

## 地景清理編輯描述

Edit this terrain sprite atlas. Keep its exact 4-column by 6-row grid, the same 24 tile meanings, the three different terrace descent directions, the bright oval-leaf Ganzai versus dark narrow-leaf Oolong, and their bare-soil versus grass variants. Keep the exact same pixel-art palette, coarse pixel size, lighting and fixed camera. Production cleanup only: EVERY tile must be wholly contained inside its equal grid cell, centered, with at least 12% fully transparent empty padding on ALL FOUR SIDES. Reduce the tiles slightly within their cells to create that padding, without changing the grid layout. Remove ALL stray detached leaf fragments, neighboring-cell debris and colored outlines/fringing around silhouettes. Each cell contains only its own complete tile and no fragment of a neighboring cell. Avoid clipping the top of the tea plants or front of the stone walls. Maintain a real transparent alpha background. Preserve all sixteen mature tea terrains (rows1-4), the forest/grassland/eroded/collapsed tiles in row5, and four young tea seedling variants in row6. No text, symbols or background scene.

## 混作生成描述

Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE production transparent pixel-art overlay sprite atlas, exact two equally sized square cells side by side, overall 2:1 aspect ratio, no gutters or frames. For a Sanxia Taiwan isometric tea farm game. Left cell: a small group of TWO pomelo flowering shrubs, dark-green oval leaves and MANY clearly visible small white five-petaled blossoms with tiny yellow centers. Absolutely NO pomelo fruit, no large yellow balls, no oranges in this cell. Right cell: a small group of TWO compact kumquat shrubs, narrow glossy green leaves and many small oval fruits with rich GOLDEN YELLOW skins, amber highlights; fruits must be yellow-gold rather than orange. Both shrub groups use the same scale, baseline, view and coherent rich 16-bit pixel art style as hillside tea-garden sprites, hard edges, crisp square pixel clusters, dark green foliage, warm ochre shading, no anti-aliased vector look, no smooth gradients. Isolated foliage, trunks and blossoms/fruit only, alpha transparent outside each shrub group. Do not draw land, soil blocks, terrace, tea bushes, pot, basket, people, wildlife, lettering or symbols. Every group stays entirely in its own equal square cell with generous transparent margins. These will be placed on top of other terrain layers.

## 輕度流失編輯描述

Edit this 4-column by 6-row pixel-art terrain atlas to create its LIGHT SOIL EROSION variant. Preserve exact canvas size, exact 24 equal cell boundaries, each block position, footprint, camera, tea cultivar distinctions, terrace step geometry and all three terrace directions. Keep hard pixel art, same colors and lighting. Add visible LIGHT topsoil loss to EVERY terrain block: several small ochre bare patches, thin brown runoff rills, slightly exposed roots, a few small stones washed downhill, mild thinning and yellowing of foliage, while clearly retaining the original mature tea rows, grass cover, forest, meadow and seedlings and their differences. Terrace stone risers remain fully intact and stair-stepped, but soil on the treads has small washed-away patches. Grass variants keep most grass, unlike bare variants. This is surface erosion, NOT collapse: do not add landslides to healthy cells, do not destroy land geometry, do not remove all crops. Existing collapsed cell remains collapsed. Keep all changes inside each original grid cell and alpha transparent outside terrain. Remove detached fragments at cell edges. All 24 cells must slice correctly with a 4x6 grid. No text, no arrows, no labels.

## 嚴重流失編輯描述

Edit this 4-column by 6-row pixel-art terrain atlas to create its SEVERE SOIL EROSION variant. Preserve exact canvas size, 24 equal cell boundaries, each block center and footprint, fixed camera, tea cultivar differences, and all three terrace directions. Keep same cohesive crisp 16-bit pixel art, hard square pixels and coherent palette. Add clearly SEVERE topsoil loss to EVERY terrain block: broad ochre and reddish-brown exposed subsoil patches, several deep downward runoff gullies, many exposed roots, displaced small stones at downslope edges, visibly thinned and yellow-brown stressed tea foliage. Retain enough surviving bright round Ganzai or dark narrow Oolong tea plants for cultivar recognition; retain some GRASS in grass variants so they still differ from bare soil. Keep terrace stone risers and their three descending directions clearly readable, with damaged or washed-away soil ON the steps. Severe erosion is NOT total collapse: retain the land footprint and the different terrace geometries. Forest retains trees with exposed roots; meadow becomes patchy; seedlings remain sparse and stressed. Existing collapsed tile remains collapsed. Every sprite stays in its own original grid cell, no neighboring fragments, alpha transparent outside terrain. No text, arrows, symbols or labels.

## 六張成果圖集生成描述

Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE production-ready pixel-art sprite atlas for six collectible achievement illustrations for a Traditional Chinese educational game about tea farming in Sanxia, Taiwan. Exactly a 3-column by 2-row grid, six equally sized square panels, no gutters, no border frames, each panel fills its square. Total image aspect ratio 3:2. No letters, no words, no numerals, no logos anywhere; UI overlays all Chinese text separately. All panels must share the SAME charming 16-bit pixel-art style, visibly square pixel clusters, hard outlines, rich but coherent greens, warm ochre, jade, muted blue, cream. No smooth vector shapes, no photorealism, no gradients or blurry brushwork. Friendly characters appropriate for elementary students, diverse adult tea farmers, warm and inviting mood, clear large subjects that remain legible as game cards. Top-left: a joyful Taiwanese tea shop owner holding a large armful of generic green banknotes and a few golden coins, wooden tea shop and stacked tea tins behind, wealthy through successful tea business. Top-middle: a tea artisan in indigo work clothes, carefully hand-rolling green tea leaves on a bamboo tray, tea baskets and warm tea workshop behind. Top-right: a farmer with a small shovel caring for very clear stepped hillside terraces, stone retaining walls, lush grass cover and a winding creek, protected soil. Bottom-left: a friendly woman organic tea farmer in a tea garden with grass between tea rows, small birds, butterflies, flowers and retained forest, happy ecological coexistence. Bottom-middle: an enthusiastic tea brand ambassador presenting a cup of tea to smiling visitors beside a quaint Sanxia-style old-street storefront, tea garden hills beyond, no signs with writing. Bottom-right: a creative young tea entrepreneur at a wooden market counter with pale green tea ice cream, golden crescent pastries and tea tins, tea experience visitors and tea garden beyond. Each panel is a standalone full composition; no crossing panel boundaries. Consistent large-pixel scale, consistent lighting, characters drawn with the same design language. This is an art atlas only, not a website mockup.

Use case: illustration-story. Create a single square collectible achievement illustration for a Traditional Chinese elementary-school educational game about Sanxia tea farming, Taiwan. Same cohesive detailed 16-bit pixel-art look as a warm Taiwanese tea shop and mountain farm: visibly square pixel clusters, hard outlines, ochre and jade palette, rich green tea hills, bright warm daylight, friendly chibi adult characters.
